status_summary: The State Department announced a reorganization on 2025-04-22 that folds the Bureau of Energy Resources into the Bureau of Economic and Business Affairs, and Fortune reported that the bureau effectively ceased to exist in July 2025 with its capabilities moved into the economic bureau, so the functions stayed within State rather than moving to DOE. H.R. 7037, the DOMINANCE Act, was introduced 2026-01-13, passed the House by voice vote on 2026-06-08 and was referred to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on 2026-06-09; it would create a State Bureau of Energy Security and Diplomacy. The DOE Office of International Affairs page and the DOE realignment release of 2025-11-20 do not describe a transfer of international energy functions, and no expanded DOE National Security Council representation or DOE embassy billets were found.

timeline.event: The Secretary of State announced a department restructuring that folds the Bureau of Energy Resources into the Bureau of Economic and Business Affairs.

The Bureau of Energy Resources effectively ceased to exist in July 2025 (month-only date), and a State Department spokesperson later confirmed its capabilities were incorporated into the economic bureau, per Fortune.
H.R. 7037, the DOMINANCE Act (Rep. Young Kim), was introduced in the House and referred to the Foreign Affairs Committee.
The House Foreign Affairs Committee ordered H.R. 7037 reported as an amended substitute by a 45-0 vote.
The House passed H.R. 7037 under suspension of the rules by voice vote; the bill would establish a Bureau of Energy Security and Diplomacy within the State Department.
H.R. 7037 was received in the Senate and referred to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee; no further action is recorded.
